newsitem.title: USA: Florida citrus belt stays dry, growth slowed.
newsitem.headline: Florida citrus belt stays dry, growth slowed.

text.p: Most areas of the Florida citrus belt were dry and cool again for the week ended Dec 1, the Florida Agricultural Statistics Service (FASS) said, with harvesting of all fruit increasing for the holiday season.
There is very little new growth and trees are slowing their growth cycles for the winter season, Fass said.
According to FASS, caretakers are cutting cover crop prior to harvesting and for fire protection.
Additionally, FASS estimated 301,000 boxes of Navel oranges were harvested in the week ended December 1, down from 344,000 boxes in the previous week and 225,000 boxes in the week ended November 17.
An estimated 4,457,000 boxes of early and mid oranges were harvested in the week ended December 1, down from 5,209,000 boxes the prior week and 2,373,000 boxes the week ended November17, FASS said.
